source_text: Tota disputatione tua contrivisti - sicut te iactas - assertionem meam, de malo carnalis concupiscentiae originalisque peccati conspiratio perditorum
pass_a_gloss: Whole in-disputation your contrivisti - as you iactas - assertionem my, about/from to-evil carnal of-desire original-and of-sin conspiracy of-the-lost.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Throughout my argument I have crushed your assertion about the evil of sexual desire and original sin.
Augustine reports that Julian claims the teaching of Basil of Caesarea and John of Constantinople agrees with his party’s views.
‘The people’s murmuring’ is the only thing you set against us.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
